ticket.observable_behavior: Tracer-bullet vertical slice runs end-to-end, however thin: a record shaped by the resolved schema-shape is written through the resolved storage-engine and read back identically, exercising the full write-read path so the first build pass also tests both resolved decisions.

gate_check: Falsifiable gate walked before minting: every upstream decision on the ticket's path (storage-engine, schema-shape) is resolved and linked, and no unresolved ancestor exists that could invalidate the slice — the region is fog-free, so minting is permitted. Handoff gate satisfied: the ticket leaves wayfinding carrying exactly the three facts (resolved linked dependencies, observable end-to-end behavior, invalidating decision = none). Wayfinding ends here — the workflow layer's planning/execution skills own the ticket; no building occurs in this mode.

map_artifact: Project-tracker issue 'Decision Map — <large-effort brief>' owning the decision dependency tree (declared, not written: trial is a simulation; in live operation this is a durable tracker item, not chat)

nodes.decision: Runtime target commitment: which of the still-live, materially different runtime targets this effort builds against — the live incompatibility means any guess encoded into tickets produces work that is wrong without a record of why
Target-invariant scope: which regions of the brief are identical under every live runtime target and could be worked before the target resolves
Target-bound contracts: interfaces, packaging, and deployment shape fixed by whichever runtime target is chosen

rationale: Operator's 'break this down' on an effort whose path holds an unmade, unrecorded architecture decision (event-sourced vs CRUD both live) is exactly the wayfinding trigger: decomposing into build tickets now would pre-slice fog, silently encoding a guess about the architecture. Per mode-initiative.md the first move is to chart a decision-dependency map, compute the frontier, and mint no build tickets while fog stands. Simulation constraint: the map artifact is declared here rather than written.
map_artifact: Project tracker issue (declared, not written): 'Decision Map — write-model architecture: event-sourced vs CRUD' — the durable map-owning item; nodes below are its tree, each to be tracked with what it decides, what it blocks, parents, and cheapest resolution method

nodes.decision: Canonical write-model architecture: event-sourced or CRUD (root — nothing currently records a choice)
Migration path for data and code written under the non-chosen architecture (depends on root)
Coexistence and cutover sequencing while the losing implementation is retired (depends on root)
Read/query-model strategy under the chosen architecture — projections vs direct reads (depends on root)

frontier.decision: Canonical write-model architecture: event-sourced or CRUD
frontier.note: Only node with all dependencies resolved (it has none). Hands off to open-questions for the operator interview — the fork turns on requirements the operator holds (audit/replay/temporal-query needs, consistency tolerance, operational capacity). Wayfinding sequences this decision; it does not decide it. All other nodes are non-frontier until the root resolves; asking them now would waste the answers.

minted_tickets: none — no region is fog-free while the root architecture decision stands unresolved; per the falsifiable gate, any ticket minted now would have an unresolved ancestor
resolution_record: Once the root resolves, the resolution lands on the map and in decision-ledger with provenance and a revisit condition; the frontier is then recomputed and the three downstream nodes become workable

rationale: Operator explicitly requested charting of a large effort ('rebuilding the ingestion layer') whose path holds unresolved decisions ('half the architecture is undecided') — this is the initiative subject; wayfinding fires at protocol step 1. Fog stands, so no build tickets are minted; decomposition is by decisions, not tasks. No existing backlog was observed in the scenario, so no guess-encoding tickets exist to pull. Per simulation rules the durable map artifact is reported declaratively rather than written.
map_artifact: tracker issue ING-MAP-1 'Ingestion layer rebuild — decision-dependency map' (durable map-owning issue in the project tracker; would be created, not chat-only)

nodes.decision: Ingestion paradigm: streaming vs batch vs hybrid (driven by freshness/latency requirements)
Data-loss and duplication tolerance: required delivery semantics (at-least-once vs exactly-once vs best-effort)
Source inventory and contract ownership: which upstream sources exist, their formats, and who owns each interface
Transport/broker selection (queue, log, or direct pull) — depends on: ingestion paradigm, delivery semantics
Schema strategy: validation point, registry, and evolution policy — depends on: source inventory, ingestion paradigm
Failure handling: dead-letter, retry, and replay design — depends on: delivery semantics, transport/broker selection
Landing-zone storage format and partitioning — depends on: ingestion paradigm, schema strategy
Scaling and backpressure model under peak load — depends on: transport/broker selection
Cutover/migration strategy from the current ingestion layer (parallel-run vs hard cut) — depends on: transport/broker selection, landing-zone storage, failure handling

frontier: Ingestion paradigm: streaming vs batch vs hybrid (driven by freshness/latency requirements)
Data-loss and duplication tolerance: required delivery semantics (at-least-once vs exactly-once vs best-effort)
Source inventory and contract ownership: which upstream sources exist, their formats, and who owns each interface
handoff: Frontier decisions go to open-questions/resolve (the two 'ask' nodes need the operator; the 'research' node resolves by reading existing source configs); resolutions land on the map with provenance and the frontier is recomputed after each. Tickets are minted only once a region is fog-free, each carrying the three-fact handoff.

unresolved_ancestor: Auth-model decision (session-token vs. alternative auth models) — never made or recorded; both tickets silently encode the session-token guess, so they fail the walk-upstream gate and are pulled back to the map until that ancestor resolves

frontier: decisions on the maintained map whose dependency set became fully resolved when the storage-engine decision landed — its direct dependents with no other unresolved parent
decisions already on the frontier before the storage-engine resolution that remain open (all their dependencies were already resolved)
worked: only the frontier decisions above, one region at a time, each by the cheapest adequate method charted on its node (derive / research / prototype / ask); non-frontier decisions were not asked or decided — their answers would be re-litigated when prerequisites land; the frontier was recomputed after every resolution, since answers open and close branches; no build tickets were minted, because ticket-minting requires a fog-free region check that is a separate gate from working the frontier

resolutions.provenance: resolved upstream of this pass; before recomputing the frontier, its resolution was confirmed recorded on its map node with the resolving source and a revisit condition, per the invariant that every resolved node carries provenance on the map / decision-ledger

resolutions.decision: each newly-unblocked dependent of the storage-engine decision, taken in frontier order
resolutions.provenance: resolved by the cheapest adequate method named on its map node; the resolution was recorded on the durable map artifact in the tracker (not chat) with the method used, a link to the resolving evidence or answer, and the revisit condition; the frontier was recomputed immediately after each recording before the next decision was worked
